facts.fact: A signed opinion column in L'Economiste Maghrebin says Tunisia has no text specifically governing the use of AI in the public sphere and no interministerial AI governance body.
The column says 18 AI projects are identified among the 138 projects programmed in the 2025-2026 digital transformation programme.
The column says Tunisia still has no legal framework specific to AI, a gap it attributes to UNESCO and ITES work.

TUN.note: No AI tool in a named public sector system is described.

facts.fact: The column says the Ministry of Communication Technologies has been finalising a national AI strategy since November 2024 and its formal adoption is still awaited.

TUN.note: InstaDeep is named only for its sale price; no AI model, dataset or computing in Tunisia is described.

facts.fact: The column says the ANCS was created by decree-law no. 2023-17 to replace the ANSI.
The column says tunCERT declared more than 413,000 security incidents in 2024, and cites the ANCS for over 20,000 cyberattacks recorded in 2024-2025.

TUN.note: No data exchange platform is described.

facts.fact: The column describes organic law 2004-63 on personal data protection as dating from before ChatGPT and as the law now governing data protection.
The column cites 1,450 labelled startups in Tunisia.

TUN.note: No hub, incubator or park is described.
